findings.issue_text: In topics_controller.rb unsubscribe action (~line 100), current_user.id is called unconditionally, causing NoMethodError/500 for anonymous users instead of a login redirect when the unsubscribe link is opened without session cookies

No request/controller spec for the new TopicsController#unsubscribe action: the regular↔muted toggle, slug-mismatch 301 redirect, and perform_show_response reuse are untested despite mutating user data (tu.save!)

Untested edge cases in TopicsController#unsubscribe: current_user nil (anonymous user raises NoMethodError) and missing TopicUser record (tu nil → tu.notification_level raises), with no test distinguishing these failure modes
No spec for new Topic#unsubscribe_url model method; a typo or URL-shape bug breaks every unsubscribe link in every email

MessageBuilder spec change verifies mocks not behavior: it adds unsubscribe_url to fixture but only asserts List-Unsubscribe header, not that %{unsubscribe_link} placeholder in HTML body is replaced, so broken html_part interpolation passes
No test for the changed perform_show_response HTML rendering path (format.html now renders :show), affecting existing show action behavior with no spec update
No frontend test for the new unsubscribe route, model hook, afterModel mutation, and template rendering (no QUnit acceptance test navigating to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe)

Untested boundary condition in the unsubscribe toggle: user already at regular level gets muted (not left at regular), and no spec pins down either branch, allowing silent inversion in future refactors

Nil TopicUser crash in unsubscribe: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when user has no topic_user record, and tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError; should use TopicUser.change abstraction instead of bypassing the model boundary

State-mutating GET endpoint /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe with no authorization or CSRF token silently changes notification level and can be triggered by link prefetchers, referer leakage, or mail forwarding; also missing current_user check so anonymous hits crash on current_user.id

Raw HTML interpolation of topic title via triple-stash {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} bypasses HTML escaping and bakes markup into the locale string, creating an injection vector if fancyTitle carries unsanitized content

Duplicated show-action logic in unsubscribe: re-implements TopicView construction, slug-mismatch redirect, and serialization, diverging from show's Discourse::InvalidAccess/guardian checks so it can operate on topics the user can't see

Fragile coupling on unsubscribe_link locale key: %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation raises MissingInterpolationArgument for any mailer using add_unsubscribe_link that doesn't pass unsubscribe_url, crashing email build

adjudication_records.issue_text: In topics_controller.rb unsubscribe action (~line 100), current_user.id is called unconditionally, causing NoMethodError/500 for anonymous users instead of a login redirect when the unsubscribe link is opened without session cookies

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code calls `current_user.id` unconditionally when doing `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])`. The diff shows no guard (e.g., `ensure_logged_in`) added for this new action; it’s also explicitly made non-XHR via `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`, making it plausible to be hit anonymously from an email link. If `current_user` is nil, this will raise `NoMethodError` and 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET request to t/:id/unsubscribe mutates notification level with no confirmation step; mail-scanner bots and link prefetching will silently change user notification state, and the state-changing GET is trivially CSRF-able

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new GET route `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (and slugged variant) mapped to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which *mutates state* by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. This is a state-changing action reachable via a plain GET link (`unsubscribe_url` is injected into notification emails), with no confirmation step and no CSRF protection shown; such GET endpoints are susceptible to link prefetching/mail scanners triggering unwanted changes and are trivially CSRF-able.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In topics_controller.rb unsubscribe, TopicUser.find_by can return nil, so tu.notification_level crashes with a 500 on a valid unsubscribe URL when the TopicUser row is absent; needs nil-check with TopicUser.change/create fallback
Unsubscribe toggle logic contradicts the email's promise: a tracking user is set to regular, which still sends notifications for direct replies, instead of going straight to muted

adjudication.rationale: The new unsubscribe messaging promises the user will “stop receiving notifications” for the topic (client: `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`, server email: “To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic”). But `TopicsController#unsubscribe` only downgrades users with `notification_level > regular` to `regular` (and only toggles to `muted` when already `<= regular`). For a tracking/watching user, clicking the unsubscribe link does not necessarily stop all topic-related notifications, contradicting the stated intent of an “unsubscribe” action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-idempotent toggle behavior: for a tracking user, first GET sets regular and a second GET sets muted, so resulting state depends on how many times the link was fetched rather than user intent

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the GET endpoint mutates state by toggling `tu.notification_level` based on its current value: if `tu.notification_level > :regular` it sets `:regular`, else it sets `:muted` (i.e., a second fetch will flip the result). For a tracking/watching user (> regular), the first GET sets regular, but a subsequent GET (now regular) will set muted, so the final state depends on how many times the unsubscribe URL is fetched rather than a single intended action. This behavior is directly visible in the new `unsubscribe` action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In lib/email/message_builder.rb html_part, %{respond_instructions} substitution is now nested inside the add_unsubscribe_link branch, so templates using respond_instructions without add_unsubscribe_link will render the literal %{respond_instructions} string

adjudication.rationale: In lib/email/message_builder.rb#html_part, the diff does not change the control flow: the `if @opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` guard remains, and the `%{respond_instructions}` substitution remains inside that same guard. The shown change is only formatting/whitespace plus spacing in `gsub!` arguments, so the claim that substitution is "now nested" (and newly broken) is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb passes a relative unsubscribe_url '/t/1234/unsubscribe' while production passes an absolute URL, so a regression producing relative links in emails wouldn't be caught

adjudication.rationale: The spec sets `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` (relative), but the diff does not show production passing an absolute URL. In production, `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, and `Topic#unsubscribe_url` is implemented as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"`—with no `Discourse.base_url` prefix or other absolutization shown in this diff. `Email::MessageBuilder` also just interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` as provided. So the claim that production uses an absolute URL (and the spec mismatches it) isn’t verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 stopNotificiationsText injects model.fancyTitle into an HTML string rendered with triple-stash unescaped output, creating a latent XSS surface if server sanitization rules change

adjudication.rationale: In the new topic-unsubscribe flow, `stopNotificiationsText` returns `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })` (controller `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`), and the template renders it via triple-stash `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (`templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`). The translated string includes raw HTML (`{{title}}` in `client.en.yml`), so `model.fancyTitle` is interpolated into an HTML string that is explicitly rendered unescaped. If `fancyTitle` ever contains unsafe HTML (now or in future changes), this becomes an XSS vector; the diff clearly introduces/depends on unescaped HTML rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET unsubscribe endpoint mutates state; email client prefetching (Gmail, Outlook, spam filters) can silently unsubscribe users before they read the email — needs confirmation step, POST, or signed token

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a state-changing unsubscribe action that is reachable via GET: routes.rb maps `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and `tu.save!`. The mailer now includes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and server locale `unsubscribe_link` renders a clickable link to that URL, so email clients/spam filters that prefetch GET links could trigger the mutation without user intent. This is a real, diff-grounded correctness/security issue (GET with side effects; no confirmation/token shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe endpoint builds and serializes a full TopicView (perform_show_response, render :show, store_preloaded) when only a cheap TopicUser.change is needed, causing unbounded per-topic cost triggered by every email link

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the action eagerly constructs `@topic_view = TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` and then calls `perform_show_response`, whose HTML branch preloads and serializes the full topic view (`store_preloaded("topic_#{@topic_view.topic.id}", MultiJson.dump(topic_view_serializer))`) and renders `:show`. This means a click on the email unsubscribe link (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`) triggers the same expensive TopicView build/serialization path as a full topic page, even though the core state change here is just toggling `TopicUser.notification_level`. That’s a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the diff, not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for users without a TopicUser record (e.g. group mention, watched category), causing NoMethodError on tu.notification_level instead of creating the record via TopicUser.change; also crashes when current_user is nil (logged-out email link click)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level`. From the diff alone, `find_by` can return `nil` (no TopicUser row), which would cause a `NoMethodError` on `tu.notification_level`. Additionally, if `current_user` is `nil` (e.g. logged-out visit), `current_user.id` will itself raise. The diff does not show any guard/requirement that a user must be logged in or that a TopicUser row must exist before this action runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe action calls TopicView.new unprotected without Discourse::InvalidAccess handling, so accessing a private/secure topic raises an unhandled error instead of the standard permission flow

adjudication.rationale: The newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action instantiates `@topic_view = TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` and immediately proceeds, but unlike the existing `show` action (which appears to have explicit exception handling around `TopicView` creation per the surrounding `rescue ex`/`raise ex` block shown in the diff), `unsubscribe` contains no `rescue Discourse::InvalidAccess` (or similar) to convert private/forbidden topic access into the normal permission/redirect response. If `TopicView.new` raises for a secure/private topic, it will bubble out of `unsubscribe` rather than following the standard flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unauthenticated, unrate-limited state-mutating GET on guessable sequential topic IDs exposes DB writes and full topic render to crawlers and prefetchers — no must_be_logged_in or rate limit

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` (and slug variant) routed to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which **mutates DB state** by toggling and `tu.save!` on `TopicUser` (notification_level) and then renders the full topic via `perform_show_response` (HTML `render :show`). Because this is a **GET with side effects**, it can be triggered by link prefetchers/crawlers/email clients or by CSRF-style inclusion while a user is logged in. However, the finding’s claim that it is “Unauthenticated / no must_be_logged_in” is not supported: `requires_login` is updated to include `:unsubscribe`, so it is login-gated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe action crashes with NoMethodError when TopicUser.find_by returns nil for users who never visited the topic; should use TopicUser.change (upsert) or handle nil

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, assigns `tu.notification_level`, `tu.save!`). If `find_by` returns `nil` (e.g., the user has no `topic_users` row for that topic), this will raise `NoMethodError`. The diff shows no nil-guard or upsert path (like `TopicUser.change`) in this action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe action has no guard for anonymous users (current_user nil) even though the route is publicly reachable and exempt from check_xhr

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the new action uses `current_user` without any nil guard (e.g., `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` and `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`). The route is newly added as a public GET endpoint (`get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) and `check_xhr` is explicitly skipped for `:unsubscribe`, so an anonymous request would plausibly reach this code path and raise (e.g., `NoMethodError` on `current_user.id`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe_link locale string now requires %{unsubscribe_url} but only send_notification_email passes unsubscribe_url, causing other mailers using add_unsubscribe_link to raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument

adjudication.rationale: In `config/locales/server.en.yml`, `unsubscribe_link` was changed to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, the unsubscribe snippet is always generated via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but `template_args` only has `user_preferences_url` by default and does not define `unsubscribe_url` unless a caller passes it via opts (`.merge!(@opts)`). The diff updates `send_notification_email` and the message_builder spec to pass `unsubscribe_url`, implying it’s now required; any other use of `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` would raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe is a state-mutating GET endpoint without CSRF/token; prefetchers and link scanners (e.g. Outlook SafeLinks) will silently mute topics; needs a confirmation page instead of auto-muting

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` routes to `topics#unsubscribe` (config/routes.rb). The `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action mutates state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` based solely on the GET request (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb). There is no CSRF/token check shown, and because it’s a GET endpoint, Rails’ CSRF protections typically don’t apply—making it vulnerable to link prefetchers/scanners triggering the change. Although a client-side unsubscribe page/template is added, the mutation happens before rendering, so simply visiting/scanning the link toggles/mutes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 301 permanent redirect from slugless email link to slug URL re-performs the mutation on the destination, compounding the GET mutation issue with cached redirects

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the 301 redirect happens *before* any mutation: the method returns immediately when `params[:slug].blank?` (for non-JSON) via `redirect_to ... status: 301`, and only after that block does it toggle `TopicUser.notification_level` and `save!`. So a slugless request does not perform the mutation and therefore cannot “re-perform” it on the destination due to the redirect. Also, the email code sets `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, and `Topic#unsubscribe_url` is based on `url` (typically the canonical/slugged URL), so the premise of a slugless email link is not shown by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale email links may hit nil @topic_view.topic causing NoMethodError instead of a clean 404

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code sets `@topic_view = TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` and then uses `@topic_view.topic` (e.g., `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url`). The diff does not show `TopicView.new` ever returning an object with `topic == nil`; in typical Rails patterns a missing topic would raise (e.g., `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`) and be handled as a 404 by higher-level rescue, not produce a `NoMethodError`. The claimed nil `@topic_view.topic` path is therefore not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client route /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe may mismatch server URL shape (slug vs numeric topic id positions), risking wrong record load in Ember's model hook

adjudication.rationale: The Ember route path is `'/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe'` and the Rails route is `t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` (also `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`). The URL *shape/segment order* matches (slug first, numeric id second); only the parameter name differs (`id` vs `topic_id`), which is internal to each router and does not affect parsing. The Ember model hook correctly uses `params.id` for the second segment, which corresponds to the numeric topic id in the server route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation in server.en.yml unsubscribe_link breaks all mailers that pass add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url (signup emails, digest, user mailer etc.), raising I18n::MissingInterpolationValue or emitting literal placeholder and breaking email delivery sitewide

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it unconditionally does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`, and `template_args` only contains `site_name`, `base_url`, and `user_preferences_url` by default (plus whatever the caller passed in `@opts`). There is no default `unsubscribe_url`, so any existing caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also providing `unsubscribe_url` will trigger `I18n::MissingInterpolationValue` (or equivalent broken output) at render time. The spec update adding `unsubscribe_url` supports that a new required interpolation was introduced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unauthenticated user clicking email unsubscribe link gets a 500 (NoMethodError on nil.id in TopicsController#unsubscribe) because there is no login requirement before_filter; should redirect to login

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `:unsubscribe` to the controller’s `requires_login` list in `TopicsController` (near the top: `... :bookmark, :unsubscribe]`). That implies unauthenticated requests should be intercepted/redirected by the existing login filter rather than reaching `current_user.id` and 500ing in `#unsubscribe`. While `#unsubscribe` does call `current_user.id`, the finding’s premise (“no login requirement before_filter”) is contradicted by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tu can be nil in TopicsController#unsubscribe (TopicUser.find_by with no record, e.g. notification via group/watched-category defaults or record deleted) causing NoMethodError and 500; should use TopicUser.change/upsert semantics

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and assigns `tu.notification_level = ...` without checking for `nil`. If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic (possible when defaults apply or the row was deleted), this will raise `NoMethodError` and return a 500. The diff introduces this new action and the nil-unsafe access is visible in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bare save! inside a GET request in TopicsController#unsubscribe with no rescue or error handling surfaces raw 500s and skips MessageBus notification-level-change publish that TopicUser.change would emit

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the new GET route (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`) mutates state by directly setting `tu.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` without using `TopicUser.change`, which elsewhere publishes a `MessageBus` `notification_level_change` event. That omission is verifiable in the diff and could lead to other sessions not receiving live updates, but whether a MessageBus publish is required for this email-driven flow isn’t provable from the diff alone. The claim about surfacing raw 500s is also speculative (Rails will 500 on an exception, but the diff doesn’t show expected failure conditions).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Frontend PostStream.loadTopicView promise in topic-unsubscribe route has no .catch/error handling, leaving users on a blank/broken route on 404, permission denied, or network failure

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the `model(params)` hook calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` and does not add any `.catch(...)` nor define an `error` action on the route. The diff therefore supports the specific claim that there is no explicit error handling for 404/permission/network failures in this route. However, the finding’s assertion that this will leave users on a “blank/broken route” is not verifiable from the diff alone because Ember/Discourse may have global route error substates/handlers that render an error page on rejected model promises.

adjudication_records.issue_text: afterModel in topic-unsubscribe route assumes details is present; topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null) throws if JSON payload lacks details, breaking route transition

adjudication.rationale: In the new `topic-unsubscribe` route, `afterModel(topic)` unconditionally does `topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null);`. In Ember, setting a nested path can error if the intermediate object (`details`) is `null/undefined`. The diff doesn’t show that `topic.updateFromJson(json)` always populates `details`, so this is a concrete edge-case robustness concern but not a verifiable, guaranteed break from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Slug-redirect logic in unsubscribe can loop when topic has nil/empty slug, since the 301 redirect to unsubscribe_url may reproduce the same slugless path

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, HTML requests with a blank `params[:slug]` always 301 redirect to `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url` (`if slugs_do_not_match || (!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?) ... redirect_to ...`). A slugless route is explicitly added (`get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`), so if `Topic#url` (used by `Topic#unsubscribe_url` = `"#{url}/unsubscribe"`) can ever produce a slugless canonical URL (e.g., topic slug nil/empty), the redirect target would equal the current slugless path and the action would redirect indefinitely. The diff doesn’t show `Topic#url` behavior, so the loop condition depends on that, but the redirect logic is consistent with the reported risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Typo'd property stopNotificiationsText in topic-unsubscribe controller and template is fragile under refactoring, and triple-stash {{{...}}} renders fancyTitle HTML unescaped, a potential XSS vector if fancy_title sanitization is bypassed

No request/controller spec for the new TopicsController#unsubscribe action: the regular↔muted toggle, slug-mismatch 301 redirect, and perform_show_response reuse are untested despite mutating user data (tu.save!)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that mutates `TopicUser` state (`tu.notification_level` toggle and `tu.save!`), includes redirect logic on slug mismatch, and reuses `perform_show_response`, but the PR diff does not add any corresponding request/controller specs covering these behaviors (only an email `MessageBuilder` spec change is shown). This is a concrete, nontrivial new code path handling user data without test coverage in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Untested edge cases in TopicsController#unsubscribe: current_user nil (anonymous user raises NoMethodError) and missing TopicUser record (tu nil → tu.notification_level raises), with no test distinguishing these failure modes

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code assumes a logged-in user and an existing `TopicUser` row: `current_user.id` is called (`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`) and then `tu.notification_level` is accessed without nil checks. From the diff, the route `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` is publicly reachable and there is no shown `before_filter`/guard requiring authentication, so an anonymous request would raise `NoMethodError`, and a missing `TopicUser` record would raise on `tu.notification_level`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec for new Topic#unsubscribe_url model method; a typo or URL-shape bug breaks every unsubscribe link in every email

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `Topic#unsubscribe_url` method (`app/models/topic.rb`: `"#{url}/unsubscribe"`) and uses it to populate `unsubscribe_url` in notification email opts (`app/mailers/user_notifications.rb`). The only spec change hardcodes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` (`spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb`) and does not exercise or validate `Topic#unsubscribe_url` against the actual route shape. However, the claim that there is a typo/URL-shape bug breaking every link is not verifiable from the diff: the method appears consistent with the new routes (`/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No mailer spec verifying the unsubscribe URL reaches the rendered email; existing user_notifications specs not updated to assert the per-topic link in the body, so a dropped %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation would go uncaught

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new per-topic unsubscribe URL into the email pipeline (user_notifications passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`; server locale `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`; `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` renders it via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`), but the only shown spec change (`spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb`) merely supplies `unsubscribe_url` without asserting that the rendered HTML body actually contains the link/URL. No other mailer/body assertion updates are visible in this diff, so a regression where `%{unsubscribe_url}` is omitted/mis-interpolated in the rendered email body could go uncaught. This is a test coverage gap rather than a proven functional bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MessageBuilder spec change verifies mocks not behavior: it adds unsubscribe_url to fixture but only asserts List-Unsubscribe header, not that %{unsubscribe_link} placeholder in HTML body is replaced, so broken html_part interpolation passes

adjudication.rationale: In the shown spec diff, the only change is adding `unsubscribe_url` to the `message_with_unsubscribe` fixture, while the visible example still only asserts the `List-Unsubscribe` header. Meanwhile the diff expands the server-side `unsubscribe_link` translation to include `%{unsubscribe_url}` and `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` performs string substitution of `%{unsubscribe_link}` into the HTML. Based on what’s visible here, there is no test assertion that the cooked unsubscribe text (including the new topic-specific link) is actually interpolated into the HTML body, so a regression in `html_part` substitution could go uncaught.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for the changed perform_show_response HTML rendering path (format.html now renders :show), affecting existing show action behavior with no spec update

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `TopicsController#perform_show_response` to explicitly `render :show` inside the `format.html` block (previously it relied on implicit rendering). That is a behavioral change for any action that calls `perform_show_response` (notably the newly added `unsubscribe` action also calls it), and the diff does not add/update any controller/request spec to assert the HTML template rendering behavior for this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No frontend test for the new unsubscribe route, model hook, afterModel mutation, and template rendering (no QUnit acceptance test navigating to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new Ember route/controller/template for topic unsubscribe (e.g., `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` with `model` + `afterModel` mutation, `controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, and `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`) and wires it into the client route map (`app-route-map.js.es6`). The only test change shown is a Ruby spec update for `Email::MessageBuilder` (`spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb`); there are no frontend/QUnit acceptance tests added in this diff that exercise navigating to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` or validate the route’s model loading / `afterModel` behavior / template rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Untested boundary condition in the unsubscribe toggle: user already at regular level gets muted (not left at regular), and no spec pins down either branch, allowing silent inversion in future refactors

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new toggle logic in `TopicsController#unsubscribe`: it sets `tu.notification_level` to `:regular` if the current level is `> :regular`, otherwise it sets it to `:muted` (so a user already at `:regular` will be moved to `:muted`). This behavior is not covered by any new spec in the diff (the only added spec change is in `message_builder_spec` for `unsubscribe_url`), so neither branch of the toggle is pinned down and could be silently changed/inverted in future refactors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Nil TopicUser crash in unsubscribe: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when user has no topic_user record, and tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError; should use TopicUser.change abstraction instead of bypassing the model boundary

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` when the user has no `topic_users` row for that topic (e.g., user got an email but never visited). The next line `tu.notification_level > ...` will then raise `NoMethodError` on `nil`. The diff shows no guard/creation path (e.g., `TopicUser.change`), so this is a real crash scenario introduced by the new action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: State-mutating GET endpoint /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe with no authorization or CSRF token silently changes notification level and can be triggered by link prefetchers, referer leakage, or mail forwarding; also missing current_user check so anonymous hits crash on current_user.id

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds GET routes `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (config/routes.rb) mapped to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which mutates state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb). Because it's a GET, it bypasses normal CSRF protections for state changes and can be triggered unintentionally by link prefetchers or crawlers. Additionally, the action dereferences `current_user.id` without any visible login/authorization guard; if `current_user` is nil, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)` will raise, matching the finding's anonymous-crash concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw HTML interpolation of topic title via triple-stash {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} bypasses HTML escaping and bakes markup into the locale string, creating an injection vector if fancyTitle carries unsanitized content

adjudication.rationale: The new template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (triple-stash), which bypasses Handlebars HTML escaping. That string is built in `controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` via `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`, and the locale `client.en.yml` includes raw HTML (`{{title}}`). As shown in the diff, this will output `model.fancyTitle` into HTML without escaping, so if `fancyTitle` can contain unsafe content this is an XSS/injection vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated show-action logic in unsubscribe: re-implements TopicView construction, slug-mismatch redirect, and serialization, diverging from show's Discourse::InvalidAccess/guardian checks so it can operate on topics the user can't see

adjudication.rationale: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` largely reuses the same building blocks as `show` (it constructs `TopicView.new`, does a slug-mismatch redirect, and then calls `perform_show_response`). However, it does so as a separate action with its own flow, which can easily drift from `show`’s access/exception handling (e.g., `show`’s surrounding rescue/invalid-access handling is not present in `unsubscribe` in this diff). The specific claim that it "can operate on topics the user can't see" is not directly verifiable from the diff because `TopicView.new(..., current_user)` may already enforce visibility, but the duplication/divergence risk is real and grounded in the added action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fragile coupling on unsubscribe_link locale key: %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation raises MissingInterpolationArgument for any mailer using add_unsubscribe_link that doesn't pass unsubscribe_url, crashing email build

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true it always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` with no default `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args` unless a caller passes it via opts. The diff updates one caller (`user_notifications.rb`) and one spec to provide `unsubscribe_url`, but the diff does not show (or prove) that *all* other uses of `add_unsubscribe_link` also pass it. This creates a fragile/BC-breaking coupling: any existing call site that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` would raise `MissingInterpolationArgument` at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Misspelled property stopNotificiationsText propagated through controller, template, and references, creating hidden coupling where a rename of one occurrence silently breaks the binding
matched_golden_ids: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the property name `stopNotificiationsText` is misspelled and notes its propagation across the codebase, which corresponds directly to the golden issue that it should be `stopNotificationsText` (missing 'n' in Notifications).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Drive-by reformat churn unrelated to the feature (topic_user.rb, notification.html.erb re-indent, message_builder.rb, topic-from-params.js.es6) inflates the diff, hurts git blame, and mixes mechanical rewrites with a behavior-bearing template change

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes multiple formatting/modernization-only edits unrelated to the new unsubscribe feature, e.g. Ruby style/indent changes in `app/models/topic_user.rb` (block-to-one-liner, hash syntax/spacing), large whitespace/indent refactor in `app/views/email/notification.html.erb`, restructuring/indent changes in `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, and ES6 refactors in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-from-params.js.es6`. These changes are largely mechanical and mixed into a behavior-bearing PR, which does inflate the diff and complicate blame/review even though it’s not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route placement collision with Ember nested-resource structure: topicUnsubscribe route declared as sibling of topic resource, with naming split across topic.unsubscribe, topicUnsubscribe, and topic-unsubscribe conventions making future additions easy to misplace

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent Ember naming/structure: the router declares `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` as a top-level sibling (next to `topicBySlug`), while the implementation files are in dash form (`routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`) and the template is placed as if it were a nested route (`templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, i.e. `topic.unsubscribe`). This split between `topicUnsubscribe` vs `topic-unsubscribe` vs `topic/unsubscribe` is a concrete maintainability/architecture issue and makes it easy to misplace future related routes/templates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe method crashes on nil current_user when a logged-out visitor (e.g., expired session from an email link) hits it — NoMethodError → 500; should redirect to login or render a friendly page

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code assumes `current_user` is present: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)` will raise `NoMethodError` if `current_user` is `nil` (e.g., logged-out/expired session visitor following the new `unsubscribe_url` link added to emails). The diff shows no `before_filter`/guard to require login for `:unsubscribe` (it is newly added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` and to routes), so the crash scenario is directly supported by the new action implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe method crashes when TopicUser.find_by returns nil (user never visited/tracked the topic) — tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError
matched_golden_ids: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: TopicUser.find_by may return nil when no record exists, and subsequent calls on tu (e.g., tu.notification_level) will raise a NoMethodError/nil pointer exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe is a state-mutating GET with no CSRF protection or per-user token — vulnerable to GET-based CSRF (img tag silently muting a logged-in user) and email-scanner/proxy prefetch silently unsubscribing users; no confirmation before the mutation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (config/routes.rb), and implements `TopicsController#unsubscribe` that mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` for `current_user` and `save!`s it (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb). This is a state-changing action performed via GET with no per-user/token parameter or confirmation flow shown in the diff, making it triggerable by cross-site GET requests (e.g., an `` tag) and vulnerable to unintended execution by link prefetch/email scanners. Nothing in the diff adds CSRF protection for this GET endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mutation happens before/without authorization checks and doesn't validate the user had a subscription — can silently mute a topic the user was merely at 'regular' on, hiding @mentions and replies

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code mutates `TopicUser` state without validating a `TopicUser` record exists: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` is used immediately as `tu.notification_level`, which will raise if `tu` is `nil`. Also, the logic explicitly mutes users who are at `regular` (or lower): `if tu.notification_level > ...[:regular]` then set to `regular` else set to `muted`, so the “unsubscribe” endpoint can change a merely-regular topic to muted (not just “stop emails”), matching the finding’s core concern about unintended muting. The claim about authorization is less directly verifiable from the diff (there is `requires_login` added), but the missing existence/validation and the regular→muted mutation are grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller writes tu.notification_level directly instead of TopicUser.change, so the notification_level_change MessageBus message isn't published — other open tabs keep stale state until reload

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the PR updates `tu.notification_level` directly and calls `tu.save!` (`app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`), rather than using `TopicUser.change(...)`. The diff shows `TopicUser.change` is responsible for publishing the `MessageBus` `notification_level_change` event when `attrs[:notification_level]` is present (`app/models/topic_user.rb`). By bypassing `TopicUser.change`, this action will not publish that message, so any clients relying on the bus to update notification state (e.g., other open tabs) can remain stale until reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_show_response now unconditionally renders :show in format.html, an untested behavioral change that may break the normal #show action's HTML rendering

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `render :show` inside `perform_show_response`’s `format.html` block (TopicsController), but there’s nothing in the diff showing this would break `#show`’s normal HTML rendering—explicitly rendering `:show` is consistent with the `show` action’s template. Also, whether it’s “untested” cannot be verified from the diff. The finding’s claimed risk is speculative rather than a diff-verifiable issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: slug-mismatch redirect uses permanent 301 status; when topic slug changes, old emailed links keep redirecting to dead URLs due to browser caching — should be 302/303

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, slug mismatch triggers `redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301`. This diff newly introduces a permanent (301) redirect for emailed unsubscribe links when the slug doesn’t match. While the redirect will work initially, using 301 can be cached by browsers/clients, which can cause stale redirect behavior if the canonical URL changes again; a temporary redirect (302/303) would avoid that caching risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dropdown-button.js.es6 conditional title change silently alters every dropdown-button instance; falsy titles from other callers cause the header to vanish

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `dropdown-button` rendering from always emitting `<h4 class='title'>` (even when `this.get('title')` is `null/""/undefined`) to emitting it only when `title` is truthy (`if (title) { ... }`). This is a global behavior change for all callers and could affect layout/spacing or any usage that relied on an empty title header being present, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it’s a definite defect (it may be intentional to avoid rendering `undefined`/empty headers).

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.createRecord('topic', { id: params.id }) creates a phantom record that pollutes the Ember store with no cleanup on partial failure

adjudication.rationale: In the new `topic-unsubscribe` route, `model(params) { const topic = this.store.createRecord("topic", { id: params.id }); return PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...); }` creates a new unsaved record up front. If `PostStream.loadTopicView` rejects (network/server error) or the transition is aborted before `updateFromJson` runs, the created record is left in the Ember Data store with no `unloadRecord`/rollback cleanup shown in the diff. That can leave a stale/phantom `topic` with that `id` in the store and potentially interfere with later lookups. This is a concrete diff-grounded concern, but it’s more of an error-handling/architecture issue than a guaranteed broken behavior in the happy path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Typo 'stopNotificiationsText' (extra 'i') in a public API string; also triple-stash raw HTML interpolation of fancyTitle into i18n string is a potential XSS sink if fancyTitle is unsanitized

adjudication.rationale: The new template renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (triple-stash) and the controller builds it via `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`, where the translation includes HTML (`{{title}}`). This introduces an unescaped HTML interpolation of `model.fancyTitle` into the DOM, which is a potential XSS sink if `fancyTitle` is not guaranteed sanitized. The misspelling `stopNotificiationsText` is present but is used consistently in the new template/controller, so it’s not verifiably breaking by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent UX: server HTML for /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe renders a full topic render with notification level already mutated, so some users see no confirmation page while redirect-flow users do

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicsController#unsubscribe` always ends in `perform_show_response`, whose HTML branch explicitly `render :show`, i.e., it serves the standard Ember app shell. The client-side router adds an Ember route for `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` (`topicUnsubscribe`) with its own template (`topic/unsubscribe.hbs`), so the confirmation page is expected to be rendered client-side regardless of whether there was an initial redirect (e.g., from `/t/:id/unsubscribe`). The claim that some users will see a full topic render while redirect-flow users see a confirmation page is not demonstrated by the diff; both flows ultimately serve the same `:show` HTML shell at a URL that matches the Ember unsubscribe route.
